newsitem.title: UK: UK retailer puts warning labels on alcoholic drink.
newsitem.headline: UK retailer puts warning labels on alcoholic drink.

text.p: The Co-op, a British supermarket chain, said on Monday it would put health warnings on the labels of 240 of its own-brand wines, beers and spirits to inform the public about daily guidelines for alcohol consumption.

The Co-op is the first British retailer to take such a stance, which it said it was doing despite knowingly breaching European Union regulations designed to harmonise the labelling of products across member countries.

"We have become the first retailer to put clear warnings on alcoholic drinks in order to cut through public confusion and give people the information they need to drink sensibly," a spokeswoman for the Co-op said.
The new labels will appear across alcoholic drinks in the Co-op's 2000 stores in time for Christmas.

The spokeswoman said "as a responsible retailer, we have a duty to end consumer confusion. Effectively our message is, 'Enjoy alcohol, but don't abuse it'. Retailers and manufacturers have a unique opportunity to put this message across on products themselves and we hope that others will follow our lead."

The Co-op's move has been welcomed by the Government's Health Education Authority. Its chief executive, Seymour Fortescue, said "the new alcohol labelling provides helpful, up to date health advice for consumers and sets an excellent example for the retail sector".
The Co-op said a study it had commissioned showed many people were poorly informed about effects of alcohol consumption.
It said more than 70 percent of consumers surveyed were unaware of or underestimated the alcoholic strength of alcoholic soft drinks known as "alcopops".

The Co-op says it takes an ethical approach to retailing. In the past it has introduced a new labelling scheme for battery farmed eggs which it describes as "intensively produced" rather than "farm fresh" - a description used by some other retailers.
